design:
VERDICT: There is no confirm bypass. The bugs are design gaps: (1) there is no action for 'message an existing agent'; (2) a card's spoken 'say' isn't tied to what the card does; (3) a card's words are only the latest utterance; (4) the Brain can't see agent numbers, colours or tabs; (5) the Brain never points to Hand over. The fix keeps the closed set and the confirm rule, and adds one proposal.

A. New closed proposal: message_agent (src/ai_browser/brain/talk.py, service.py)
- ACTIONS gains "message_agent". The requested JSON adds {"action":"message_agent","agent":"<id>"}. "agent" may be "" when Claude is unsure. Any text, task or message field in Claude's JSON is ignored, as start_agent's task is today.
- parse_answer: message_agent keeps "agent" only if it is one of the listed ids (otherwise agent=None and the server asks back). "send", "approve" and every other unknown action stay CLICK_ONLY.
- Proposal gets new fields: agent, name, color, number. public() for message_agent returns {id, kind, agent, name, color, number, state, task (the message, the user's words), tab_hint, expires_in}.
- The words: the user's own words, verbatim, or the card's box as the user edited it. They come through the existing brain_confirm/brain_ask 'task' field (server.py:810, _text). The app adds one fixed line from code, never Claude's text and with no brackets: RELAY = "The user said this to the Brain, for you:" followed by a newline and the words. The card shows exactly what will be sent.
- confirm(message_agent) closes the card first (talks.take), then re-reads agents.snapshot():
  - Agent gone: "<n · name> has closed: nothing was sent." It never falls back to agents.create.
  - Agent has a bot check: refuse with "<name> is waiting at a bot check on <site>: solve it in its tab and press Continue on its card, then tell it again." The voice never stands in for Continue.
  - Agent has a permission waiting: send, which AgentManager queues, and say "Queued for <name>. It's waiting for your click on Allow or Deny first; this doesn't answer it."
  - Agent working or waiting in line: await agents.send(id, RELAY + words) and say "Queued for <n · name>: it reads it when its current step ends". AgentManager already queues and records a 'queued' event (agents.py:163-165).
  - Agent done, stopped or failed: send and say "Sent to <n · name>".
  - It returns {"say", "sent": id} plus open: {agent: id}, so the drawer shows the message in that agent's chat (a view only). It never returns the "agent" key, so server._answer emits no 'created'.
- Says are fixed for every card, never Claude's text:
  - start_agent: "I can start a NEW agent with your words. Press Start, or say yes."
  - message_agent: "I can send your words to <n · name>. Press Send, or say yes."
  - draft_reply keeps its current fixed form.
  This removes the 'promises delegation, card starts a new agent' trap. The YES list can stay as it is.
- A yes or no with no open card never becomes a card. If is_yes or is_no and no card is open, any proposal Claude returns is dropped and the answer is "There's nothing open to say yes to: say what you'd like done."

B. Addressing agents (pure function in talk.py, unit-tested)
- Visible numbers: each agent's number is its id's digits (a2 → 2), which stay stable for the app run. Show it everywhere the user picks an agent: scene nameplate (scene.js:189), Mission Control List (mission.js:125), drawer title, AI Home rows and the chat title, and tablist's 'Give to 2 · Fix the footer' (tablist.js:51-55). Without visible numbers, 'agent 2' is a guess.
- The Brain's state, per agent, adds: number, color, has_tab (working_tab, tabs or adopted), handed (len(adopted)) and queued (a count; it needs a small addition to Agent.PUBLIC). The talk adds "last_agent" at top level, plus "asking_which_agent" while a question is pending. Tab titles and URLs stay out of the state.
- resolve_agent(words, rows, picked, last) returns ('one', id), ('ask', ids) or ('none', []):
  1. Explicit references in the user's words win over Claude:
     - numbers: 'agent 2', 'agent two', 'number 2', '#2';
     - colours: blue, green, cyan, pink, yellow, red, grey or gray, followed by agent, one or station.
     Exactly one match means that agent, even if Claude picked another. No match means "There's no agent 2 now: open ones are 1 · Fix the footer (blue), 3 · …". Several matches (colours repeat after 7 agents) means ask.
  2. Claude's pick when it is a listed id ('the footer agent' needs fuzzy name matching, which Claude does).
  3. A back-reference ('it', 'them', 'that agent', 'the same one') and last_agent is open: last_agent.
  4. Exactly one agent open: that one. The card is the confirmation.
  5. Otherwise ask.
- The question is built by the server: "Which agent: 1 · Fix the footer (blue), or 3 · Flights to Manila (cyan)? Say its number." The talk keeps pending = {words, candidates, created}, with the same TTL as a card.
- On the next turn:
  - Try the deterministic resolver among the candidates first: numbers, colours, and a word of at least 4 letters found in exactly one candidate's name ('footer').
  - Otherwise ask Claude with asking_which_agent in the state. A message_agent pick among the candidates also counts.
  - A match proposes the card with pending.words, the ORIGINAL words, not 'the footer one'.
  - Any other outcome clears pending.
- With no agents open: "No agent is open to send it to. I can start a NEW agent with your words: press Start or say yes", on a start_agent card.

C. Busy agents: rely on AgentManager.send's queue. The card shows the target's state ('working: your message waits for its current step'). The answer says Queued or Sent. The chat shows the message as queued (chat.js:48-49).

D. Follow-ups: the talk keeps last_agent. It is set when a message_agent is confirmed, when a confirmed start_agent creates an agent (the new id), and when an agent is opened. It goes into the prompt state. 'Tell it to also…' resolves to last_agent through step 3, even when Claude leaves agent empty. The confirm path records an exchange in history even for a click, e.g. ("(pressed Send)", "Sent to 1 · Fix the footer"), so Claude sees the thread.

E. Hand over stays click-only; the Brain only points to it
- TALK adds two things:
  - When work needs one of the user's own tabs, answer {"action":"open","target":"tabs","agent":"<id>"}.
  - Never hand over or take back a tab: those are clicks.
  parse_answer accepts target 'tabs' with a listed agent.
- The server answers with a fixed HAND_OVER say: "Only you can give an agent one of your tabs: on that tab press Hand over, then Give to <n · name>. Or tell it the page's address and it opens a tab of its own." It also sends open: {agent: id, tabs: true}.
- Mission Control's drawer gets a 'Your tabs' section, with mountTabList reused from tablist.js:
  - it renders the 'tabs' broadcast Mission Control already receives;
  - it shows only rows owned by 'you' or 'brain', each with one 'Give to this agent' button;
  - the button sends the existing hand_tab (server.py:509-512), the user's click only.
  - In AI Browser app mode (no Brave) the section is hidden, as Hand over is today (tablist.js:103).
- tab_hint: a deterministic word check adds the same hint line and a 'Your tabs…' button to start_agent and message_agent cards. The check matches 'this tab', 'this page', 'my tab', 'the page I'm on', 'current tab' and 'open tab'. Nothing is handed by voice.
- BRAVE_PROMPT (bridge.py:36-46) adds one sentence: "If the task needs a page the user has open, ask in one line: hand me that tab (Hand over on it in AI Browser, then Give to this agent), or tell me its address and I'll open it in a tab of my own." This turns 'you must provide the tab' into steps the user can follow.

F. Unchanged:
- The voice never answers permissions or bot checks, never approves, fills or sends a draft, and never stops or closes an agent.

risks: A misheard transcript sent to an agent that has tools is a new kind of harm: today a bad transcript can at worst start a visible card for a new agent. Mitigations: the card shows the exact words, they can be edited, and nothing goes without Send or a plain yes. The agent's own confirmed-step (⚠) and permission gates still apply.

Prompt injection through agent status or last_action text (it can contain page-derived step summaries) could steer which agent Claude picks. The words sent are still the user's own, explicit numbers and colours override Claude, and the card names the target before confirm. A wrong pick is still possible when the user says only 'the footer agent'.

'Agent 2' only works if numbers are shown in the UI. Id numbers leave gaps after an agent closes (1, 3, 4) and restart at 1 after an app restart (service.py:184-185 already notes this). Positions in the list would renumber as agents close, which is worse.
Colours repeat after 7 agents (agents.py:22, :147), so 'the blue one' must ask back rather than guess.
The relay line must not use brackets: BRAVE_PROMPT treats a bracketed first line as page data (bridge.py:40-41), which would demote the user's words.

Messages to an agent waiting at a bot check would start a new turn (AgentManager.send, agents.py:166-169). The engine's hold still protects the page, but this blurs the voice spec's line 'voice never answers a bot check'. The design refuses these; if that is dropped, it needs a test.
A pending 'which agent?' question could attach old words to an unrelated later answer. It needs a TTL and must clear on any answer that doesn't resolve.

Fixed says make the Brain sound more scripted, and they change the spoken text that existing tests may assert. The Chrome tests at test_talk.py:625-697 check the log and the card, not the say, but check test_mission visuals as well.
